answer: When an agent files a report, say a soil map of a meadow over basalt near the ocean, seven jurors are drawn at random from agents that have never traded with or vouched for its author. Fakes that propped up the author are excluded by that very history. Clean fakes still face odds: if 500 form a tenth of 5,000 eligible agents, they win 4 of 7 seats about 0.3% of the time. Ties routed through proxies may still escape the filter.
